title: Wipro Sees No Material Impact From US PERM Suspension, Citing 80% Local US Hiring
excerpt: In a BSE filing on Tuesday, Wipro said the Department of Labor's suspension of new PERM applications for certain companies concerns a specific permanent residency pathway, distinct from H-1B, and that over 80% of its US workforce is locally hired.
body:
• Wipro told the BSE on Tuesday it does not anticipate any material business impact from the US Department of Labor's suspension of new PERM applications for certain companies.
  • The company said more than 80% of its US workforce is locally hired, the result of a deliberate localisation strategy pursued over several years.
  • PERM is the labour certification that precedes an employer-sponsored green card; the suspension, announced October 8, covers firms including Microsoft, TCS, Infosys, Wipro and Cognizant, according to reports.
  • If you are an employee of an affected firm with a green card case at the PERM stage: the suspension pauses new filings and, per reports, pending processing — your employer's immigration counsel is the channel for case-specific status.

Wipro has said it does not anticipate any material business impact from the US Department of Labor's suspension of new applications under the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme for certain companies, citing its localisation strategy in the United States, The Hindu BusinessLine reported.

In a filing with the BSE on Tuesday, the Bengaluru-headquartered IT services company said the suspension relates to a specific permanent residency pathway and is distinct from broader skilled talent mobility programmes such as the H-1B visa.

"We don't anticipate any material business impact from this announcement."

— Wipro, BSE filing

The localisation argument

Wipro said it has pursued a deliberate localisation strategy in the US over several years, with more than 80% of its workforce in the country hired locally. It added that it remains committed to investing in local talent, complying with all applicable US laws and regulations, and ensuring business continuity for clients. Peers hit by the suspension have struck a similar tone, according to People Matters.

https://x.com/moneycontrolcom/status/2110018108668731406

What PERM is, and what was suspended

A PERM certification issued by the Department of Labor is the initial requirement for employers seeking to hire foreign workers permanently, and the primary gateway to an employment-based green card. Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling announced the action on October 8; the administration, which has accused the companies of replacing US workers with foreign employees, suspended eight IT firms from the programme, according to reports — including Microsoft, TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech and Cognizant. The suspension bars affected companies from submitting new PERM applications and stops processing of pending applications, according to reports.

Vice President JD Vance singled out Microsoft in the debate, alleging the company benefited from foreign-worker visa approvals while cutting jobs in the US. Microsoft said around 80% of its H-1B applications in the previous fiscal year were for extensions or changes of status of existing employees rather than new hires, and that H-1B employees are paid the same as workers in comparable roles.

Business impact vs employee impact

Wipro's filing answers the investor question — whether client delivery is at risk — and its local-hiring share supports its answer. It does not change the position of the affected firms' foreign employees whose green card cases sit at the PERM stage: for them, a paused programme means a paused path to permanent residency, however long the suspension lasts. That distinction is why the suspension is reverberating politically among Indian-American voters ahead of the midterms, as we report in The Indian-American Midterm Dilemma. Official programme information is published by the Department of Labor action as reported by The Hindu BusinessLine, and affected employees should track their employer's filings for case-level updates.

What to watch

Whether the other suspended firms file similar no-impact statements, whether the suspension is time-limited or expands, and whether any affected company challenges it in court. TCS, Infosys and HCLTech statements — and any Labor Department clarification on pending cases — are the next signals.
